column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “between the two evenings,” rendered “at twilight” in BSB, and repeats the command to observe it at the end.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the Passover” where BSB says “did so,” and says “between the two evenings” where BSB says “at twilight.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has “to him,” which BSB makes explicit as “to Moses,” and says “among the sons of Israel” without the supplied word “other.”
The Hebrew says “Stand, and let me hear”; BSB recasts this as “Wait here until I find out.”
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew explicitly describes a distant journey and uses “shall observe”; BSB says “away on a journey” and “may still observe.”
The Hebrew says “between the two evenings,” rendered “at twilight” in BSB, and refers to eating “it,” which BSB makes explicit as “the lamb.”
The Hebrew uses singular “a bone” and joins the prohibitions with “and”; BSB has “any of its bones” and “or.”
The Hebrew says that person must “bear his sin”; BSB expands this to “bear the consequences of his sin.”
The Hebrew states that the foreigner observes the Passover without an explicit verb “wants,” and uses singular “ordinance” where BSB has plural “ordinances.”
The Hebrew names the tabernacle three times; BSB names it twice and uses “it” for the middle occurrence.
The Hebrew does not explicitly say “by day,” which BSB supplies in contrast to the nighttime appearance.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew twice uses “the mouth of the LORD”; BSB expresses both occurrences as “the LORD’s command.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew twice uses “the mouth of the LORD”; BSB expresses these as His command.
The Hebrew has “a day and a night”; BSB gives “by day or by night.”
The Hebrew names “two days, or a month, or days”; BSB renders the last term as “longer.”
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name four times and uses the images of His mouth and Moses’ hand; BSB uses His name three times, “His command,” and “through Moses.”
